properties.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued October 5 at 6:39PM PDT until October 9 at 11:00PM PDT by NWS San Diego CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Beach Hazards Statement, dangerous rip currents
expected. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal
flooding expected.

* WHERE...San Diego County Coastal Areas and Orange County
Coastal Areas.

* WHEN...For the Beach Hazards Statement, from Tuesday afternoon
through Friday evening. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 6
AM Wednesday to 11 AM PDT Friday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of lots, parks, and roads with only isolated
road closures expected. Minor coastal erosion is also expected.
Additionally, elevated surf will lead to strong rip currents.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Elevated surf of 3-6 feet, with sets to 7
feet, on south and southwest-facing beaches. High tides are
expected to peak between 6.5 and 7.0 feet during the mornings
and evenings.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Remain out of the water to avoid hazardous swimming conditions.

properties.description:
...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in Iowa...

Wapsipinicon River near De Witt 4S affecting Clinton and Scott
Counties.

Cedar River near Conesville affecting Louisa and Muscatine
Counties.

Iowa River at Oakville affecting Louisa County.

Iowa River at Wapello affecting Louisa County.

Iowa River at Marengo affecting Benton and Iowa Counties.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring.

* WHERE...Cedar River near Conesville.

* WHEN...Until late Thursday night.

* IMPACTS...At 13.5 feet, Water affects yards and access roads of
residences along Iowa Highway 22. Water affects the lowest sections
of campgrounds just north of I-80 along the river and the lowest
sections of Jack Shuger Memorial Park in Moscow. Water is also on
152nd Street north of County Road F70.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:00 PM CDT Monday the stage was 13.5 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 13.8 feet
early tomorrow afternoon. It will then fall below flood stage
Thursday evening.
- Flood stage is 13.0 feet.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

The next statement will be issued by Tuesday evening.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 5 at 7:56PM CDT until October 7 at 1:00PM CDT by NWS Chicago IL
properties.description:
...Observed flooding changed from Minor to Moderate severity for the
following rivers in Illinois...

Des Plaines River near Russell affecting Lake IL County.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Des Plaines River from IL/WI state line downstream to US-41
in Gurnee, including the Russell gauge.

* WHEN...Until Wednesday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At 7.0 feet, Low-lying wetlands and agricultural land is
inundated near the river.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:30 PM CDT Monday the stage was 7.2 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 7:30 PM CDT Monday was 7.3 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage
Wednesday morning and continue falling through the rest of the
week.
- Flood stage is 7.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 7.2
feet on 09/20/1980.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
A Flood Warning means water levels above flood stage are imminent or
may already be occurring. Persons along rivers and streams in the
warned area should take immediate precautions to protect life and
property.

These forecasts are based almost entirely on observed precipitation
as little to no additional precipitation is currently expected over
the next 24 to 48 hours.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued by Tuesday afternoon.

Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

Additional information is available at water.noaa.gov.
